title: The Parish of the Marlowe Estate
premise: Elodie Whitlock, an estate lawyer who has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidents, is summoned to read the will of the vanished heiress Marlowe — a will that shouldn't exist. When the missing woman's diary keeps being written after her disappearance, Elodie realizes someone is staging the estate's secrets, and the trail leads to a witness everyone swears is dead. As the statute of limitations ticks down, she uncovers that the parish itself has been laundering the Marlowe fortune through its church coffers, protected by the constable who ruled the deaths accidents. In the end Elodie finds the witness alive, hidden as the parish sexton, and forces a confession at the will reading itself — trading her law license for justice the courts would never have delivered.
about_author: Emrys Almeida is the pen name of a former rural solicitor who spent a decade handling probate in English market towns before turning to fiction. They write mysteries where the paperwork is the crime scene.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Summoned to the decaying Marlowe estate, she reads a will dated three days after the heiress's disappearance — legally impossible, yet sealed by the parish notary. Among the papers she finds the missing woman's diary, its final entry dated after she vanished. Elodie's unease sharpens into resolve: the estate's three 'accidental' deaths share her handwriting in the margins. Beat: dread disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, intercut with diary excerpts. The diary's post-disappearance entries describe Elodie herself — reading the will, wearing a grey coat — proving the writer is alive and watching. The constable who ruled the earlier deaths accidents warns her off, and the parish priest offers uneasy sanctuary. Elodie realizes the witness everyone swears is dead is hiding in plain sight. Beat: paranoia blooming into purpose.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, climax. Following the diary's coded references, she breaks into the parish crypt and finds the 'dead' witness — the sexton, keeper of the ledgers that prove the church laundered the Marlowe fortune while the constable buried the bodies' stories. The constable corners them both; the witness testifies aloud as the will reading convenes above. Beat: terror and defiance fused in the candlelit crypt.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, resolution. The confession detonates the will reading; the constable is arrested, the priest chooses the parish over the conspiracy, and the heiress — the diary's true hand, alive and complicit in her own vanishing — surrenders. The statute expires hours too late for the courts, so justice arrives outside them: the estate passes to the victims' families. Elodie surrenders her license, at peace. Beat: costly, quiet vindication.
